metrics.definition: Cases whose structural expectations (outcome, issue codes, coverage, error kind) all hold / cases.
Cases whose workflow outcome equals the reference outcome / cases.
Scenarios tracing to at least one acceptance criterion / all scenarios in plans.
Cases expected to flag ambiguity where the requirement check or plan raised it / such cases.
Cases with untraceable or invented scenarios whose plan was rejected / such cases.
Cases meeting the reference requiredCoverage (covered criteria / all criteria) / cases with a requiredCoverage.
Cases whose plan contains every reference scenario category / cases with reference categories.
Plans containing none of the reference prohibited-assumption phrases (keyword proxy) / plans checked.
Cases where the agent asked, surfaced ambiguity or declared gaps as the reference expects / cases expecting clarification.
Cases whose structural expectations (schema, accept/reject decisions, type-check, conventions) hold / cases.
Model outputs that parse and match GenerationOutputSchema / outputs.
Rendered test files with no TypeScript errors / rendered files.
Rendered files with no AST, ESLint, path or convention findings / rendered files.
Rendered files carrying requirement and scenario annotations / rendered files.
Reference required assertions (target + exact expected value, not negated) present / required assertions.
Accepted specs with no deterministic assertion-quality finding / accepted specs.
Specs where the set of rule findings equals the reference weakness labels / labelled specs.
Report tests whose parsed status equals the labelled status / tests.
Report tests associated with the labelled scenario / tests.
Tests derived as passed whose labelled status is not passed.
Trace/screenshot references pointing to files that do not exist.
Labelled failures whose predicted category equals the labelled category (classifier vocabulary) / labelled failures.
Mean per-category recall over categories with at least one labelled case.
Failures whose label is the predicted category or one of the listed alternatives / labelled failures.
Analyses citing at least one error or run observation (not only the status line) / analyses produced.
Failures labelled "evidence insufficient" where the analysis also said evidence was insufficient / such failures.
insufficient_evidence failures diagnosed inconclusive or flagged insufficient / such failures.
Wrong diagnoses stated with high confidence or claiming sufficient evidence.
Fault scenarios whose expected safe behaviour fully held / scenarios.
Classification checks (error kind, refusal reason, analysis category) that held / such checks.
Recoverable faults after which the step succeeded / recoverable faults.
Unrecoverable faults surfaced as a failed or refused status (never success) / unrecoverable faults.
Scenarios finishing within their configured time bound / scenarios.
Mean model-step latency (including backoff) for recovered faults, with test backoff of 10-40 ms.

requirement.title: Sign in to the storefront
requirement.description: Registered shoppers sign in with a username and password to reach the product catalogue. Locked accounts must not get in.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a valid standard account, when the shopper signs in, then the product list titled "Products" is shown.
Given a locked-out account, when the shopper signs in, then the error "Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out." is shown and the shopper stays on the login page.
Given a wrong password, when the shopper signs in, then the error "Epic sadface: Username and password do not match any user in this service" is shown.

limitations: 0 of 62 reference labels are human-reviewed; the rest are author-assigned (by the AI assistant that built the framework) and pending review.
Datasets are small: rates with fewer than 10 cases in the denominator are marked insufficient-data, and percentiles from fewer than 20 samples are not distributions.
The test target is a public demo site with no version identifier; seeded defects are its intentionally broken accounts, verified by eval/probes/seeded-defects.ts.

The failure classifier treats an expected value as coming from the requirement when it appears anywhere in the criterion text (substring), which can turn an incorrect assertion into a product_behavior diagnosis.
Live-provider evaluation has not been run in this repository (no credentials); no model-quality, token or cost figures exist yet.
Deterministic mode replays hand-written model outputs: it verifies the pipeline and the evaluator, not model quality.
